sa-mesocricetus-auratus.title: Syrian Hamster (incl. Teddy Bear / long-haired)
sa-mesocricetus-auratus.summary: The largest and most common pet hamster, also called the golden hamster. Syrians come in many colors and coat types, including the long-haired "teddy bear". They are solitary, nocturnal burrowers that need a big enclosure with deep bedding and must live alone.
rows: Adults up to about 7 in (18 cm); usually 100–150 g, though bred lines can be larger

At least 100 × 50 cm floor (about 40 × 20 in) and 50 cm tall; bigger is better. A tank with a mesh lid works well (gaps under 1 cm). At least 20 cm (8 in) of dust-extracted paper, wood-pulp or hemp bedding for burrowing, plus hides and a sand bath. Avoid tube systems and fluffy bedding. Wheel: solid, 27–32 cm (11–12.5 in) across

Hamster pellets or a seed mix made for hamsters, with small portions of fresh vegetables (about the size of the hamster's ear); scatter food to encourage foraging. Never grapes or rhubarb. Fresh water from a bottle at all times. Small pieces of fruit as an occasional treat
Must live alone; adults are territorial and will fight
Can bite if woken or handled roughly; let it wake fully first and handle gently. Adults should supervise children
Nocturnal; most active after dark (wheel running, chewing, digging)
Arid northern Syria and southern Turkey
notes: Males grow a "skirt" of longer fur; long-haired females have shorter coats.

sa-hamster-fancy.title: Fancy Hamster (color and coat varieties)
sa-hamster-fancy.summary: A color or coat variety sold without a species name. Most pet-store hamsters are Syrian hamsters, which come in many colors, patterns and coat types; dwarf species are smaller. Either way the basics are the same: a large enclosure with deep bedding, a solid wheel, a hamster diet, and usually living alone.
rows: Syrians up to about 7 in (18 cm); dwarf species about 2.8–3.9 in (7–10 cm)

At least 100 × 50 cm floor (about 40 × 20 in) and 50 cm tall; bigger is better. A tank with a mesh lid works well (gaps under 1 cm). At least 20 cm (8 in) of dust-extracted paper, wood-pulp or hemp bedding for burrowing, plus hides and a sand bath. Avoid tube systems and fluffy bedding. Wheel: solid, at least 27–32 cm across for a Syrian (smaller for dwarfs)

Hamster pellets or a seed mix made for hamsters, with small portions of fresh vegetables (about the size of the hamster's ear); scatter food to encourage foraging. Never grapes or rhubarb. Fresh water from a bottle at all times
Syrian hamsters must live alone; dwarf pairs often fall out. Keep one hamster per enclosure unless you know the species
Can bite if woken or handled roughly; let it wake fully first and handle gently. Adults should supervise children
